comments.body:
## How this was found, and the one thing NOT proven

Found while verifying whether Gerrit change 2673 had landed. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 459e1d1b099f origin/main` returned **NO**, but the change HAD merged — as `9e6a0e436520`, found by `Change-Id`. That prompted a sweep of `is-ancestor` uses across the repo, of which this script was the only site where the rewritten sha changes an operator-visible answer.

**Not proven:** I did not establish *why* `feature/s1-windows-sweep-probe` was rebased on submit while the other four branches were not. The rebase-on-submit explanation fits (`main` is Rebase-If-Necessary, and the branch is exactly 1 commit ahead of main with its Change-Id present under a different sha), but I did not test the alternative — e.g. the branch tip being an amended patchset never submitted in that exact form, with an equivalent commit landing separately. Whoever claims this should settle that before writing the fix, because it changes whether Change-Id lookup alone is sufficient or whether patch-id equivalence is also needed.

## Store-health context from the same pass

`rebar doctor` on this store: **exit 0**, 0 stale locks, all six lock legs free, all three MCP client configs ok. Its 17 findings are all pre-existing `mis-escalated` link records (blocking-link promotion recording an endpoint that differs from the resolved comparable pair) — unrelated to this bug and not new.

Also observed and worth a separate look by whoever picks up the "checks that don't check" sweep: the CREATE of this ticket returned `push_status: {state: pending, reason: push-transport-failed, detail: "git timed out after 30s", unpushed: 3}`, i.e. three ticket commits not yet shared to `origin/tickets`. `rebar doctor` did **not** surface that condition in the output I read. I am flagging this as UNVERIFIED rather than as a finding: I read only the tail of doctor's output, so a sync section may exist above it. If it does not, "store health command does not report unshared writes" belongs in the same sweep as this bug — a store that reports healthy while three writes are invisible to every other session is the same failure shape.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## The correct pattern ALREADY EXISTS in this repo — adopt it rather than invent one

`~/.local/bin/rebar-worktree-gc.sh` (the daily worktree GC LaunchAgent) solved exactly this hazard
already, and its own header says why:

> Tier B was added 2026-08-06. Tier A alone is too strict for this repo: `main` is
> Rebase-If-Necessary, so Gerrit rewrites SHAs on submit and a [branch that landed is no longer an
> ancestor].

Its safe-to-remove predicate is two-tier:

- **Tier A** — HEAD is a true ancestor of `origin/main` (literally on main). This is the
  `is-ancestor` test `feature-branch-inventory.sh:81` uses ALONE, and the GC's own comment states
  it is insufficient for this repo.
- **Tier B** — every file the branch touched since its merge-base is **BYTE-IDENTICAL** to
  `origin/main`'s version of that file.

Tier B catches precisely the case this bug is about: a change that landed under a rewritten SHA is
no longer an ancestor, but its content is provably in main. Observed working in today's 04:00 run:

```
REMOVED fix-scanner-integration-90c7: no unlanded bytes (tier A), clean, idle
REMOVED fix-tf-fmt-9ea3:              no unlanded bytes (tier B), clean, idle
```

Both tiers firing on the same run, on real branches.

## What this changes for AC2

AC2 asks the detection to distinguish merged-via-rebase from genuinely-not-in-main. There is now a
proven in-repo implementation of that distinction, so the work is ADOPTION rather than design.

It also settles the open question this ticket recorded — whether `Change-Id` lookup suffices or
patch-id equivalence is also needed. Byte-identity of touched files is STRONGER than a `Change-Id`
match and does not depend on the trailer being present or preserved, so it answers the case I
flagged as unproven (an amended patchset never submitted in that exact form, with an equivalent
commit landing separately): content equality holds there, ancestry and `Change-Id` may not.

Note the asymmetry that makes Tier B safe in the GC's context and worth preserving here: it can
report "no unlanded bytes" for a branch whose commits differ from main, which is exactly the
desired answer, but it never reports unlanded work as landed — it compares against main's actual
file content.

## Suggested revision to the fix direction

Rather than adding a `Change-Id` lookup to `feature-branch-inventory.sh`, port the GC's two-tier
predicate: keep `is-ancestor` as the cheap fast path (MERGED-BACK), fall back to byte-identity of
touched-since-merge-base files (MERGED-REBASED), and report NOT-IN-MAIN only when both fail. That
yields the three-state output AC2 asks for, using an implementation already exercised daily on this
host against ~169 worktrees.

Cross-reference the GC script in the change so the two implementations are discoverable from each
other; a future divergence between them is the next instance of this bug.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OBSERVATION
Already had RCA; I verified the specimen. infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh classifies mergedness solely with git merge-base --is-ancestor rev main_sha. Locally, origin/main=53d18aad..., specimen tip 9c3c5ba2ea21 exists but git merge-base --is-ancestor 9c3c5ba2ea21 origin/main returns rc=1. The same tip's Change-Id Ic469bc5d6262e0be2680f0e0da17fbe3026241 is present on origin/main as 2e131f2071a0 with the same subject/body. Thus the script would label the branch ABANDONED? although the change landed under a different SHA.

HYPOTHESIS
The mechanism is SHA-ancestry identity in infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh, not content/change identity. Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary submit can rewrite the submitted commit SHA, so the pre-submit branch tip is not an ancestor of main even when the branch's work is integrated. Branches that merged without SHA rewrite are classified correctly; rebased-on-submit branches are false negatives.

CONFIRMATION
The bounded experiment used local git object/history queries only: ancestor_rc=1, both commits present, same Change-Id found in main under 2e131f2071a0. Evidence that would disprove the RCA would be the tip being an ancestor, or no equivalent Change-Id/content in main; neither held. The prior ticket comment also identified a working in-repo comparison: rebar-worktree-gc.sh already uses a two-tier ancestry then byte-identity predicate.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Design-free adoption candidate: keep is-ancestor as MERGED-BACK fast path, then fall back to the GC's touched-file byte-identity/content-equivalence check and report MERGED-REBASED separately from NOT-IN-MAIN. Also document that deletion is age/owner driven or gate deletion on state.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`infra/gerrit/feature-branch-inventory.sh:81` decides whether a feature branch has landed with:

```sh
if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$rev" "$main_sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    state="MERGED-BACK"
else
    state="ABANDONED?"   # not in main's history — either in-flight or truly abandoned
fi
```

`main` is **Rebase-If-Necessary**, so Gerrit rebases server-side on submit and the merged commit carries a **different sha** from the branch tip. `is-ancestor` on the pre-rebase tip then returns non-zero and a fully-merged branch is labelled `ABANDONED?`.

## Reproduced on live data (not reasoned)

Run 2026-09-05 against `origin/main = 4c9940348148`, comparing the script's predicate against a Change-Id lookup:

```
feature/grounding-t2            MERGED-BACK  tip=709a46e9dbda  ahead=0  change_id_in_main=YES (709a46e9dbda)
feature/idea-status             MERGED-BACK  tip=6a28e9a5a6d7  ahead=0  change_id_in_main=YES (6a28e9a5a6d7)
feature/llm-provider-seam       MERGED-BACK  tip=5f00bf5253ee  ahead=0  change_id_in_main=YES (5f00bf5253ee)
feature/oss-readiness           MERGED-BACK  tip=c4c172914825  ahead=0  change_id_in_main=YES (c4c172914825)
feature/s1-windows-sweep-probe  ABANDONED?   tip=9c3c5ba2ea21  ahead=1  change_id_in_main=YES (2e131f2071a0)
```

**`feature/s1-windows-sweep-probe` is the specimen.** Its tip's `Change-Id` is present in `main` as `2e131f2071a0` ("Make the Windows exclusive-leg tests runnable") — the work fully landed — yet the inventory reports `ABANDONED?`. The four branches that label correctly simply were not rebased on submit, which is why the defect is intermittent rather than total.

## Severity — deliberately p3, and why

The error direction is **conservative**. `is-ancestor` under-reports merges; it cannot report an unmerged branch as merged, so nothing here can mark live work safe to delete. Further, `--delete` is gated on **age** (`CAP_DAYS`) plus owner confirmation and does NOT consult `state` at all, so the mislabel does not gate any destructive action.

The real cost is misdirection: an operator or agent reading `ABANDONED?` for work that already landed may believe the work was lost and attempt to preserve or re-land it — wasted effort, and a duplicate-landing risk. There is a secondary observation worth recording: the computed `state` currently has no effect on the only destructive path, so the check informs a human and nothing else.

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

Determine merged-ness by content/identity rather than by ancestry: look up the tip's `Change-Id` in `main`, or use `git cherry` / `git patch-id` to detect the rebased equivalent. Keep `is-ancestor` as the fast path and fall back when it says no. Distinguish three states rather than two — MERGED-BACK / MERGED-REBASED / NOT-IN-MAIN — so "rebased and landed" is not conflated with "abandoned".

## Related, and NOT affected

The ticket close precheck is immune: it scans for a `rebar-ticket:` trailer on a reachable commit (`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`), not for a specific sha, so a rebase-on-submit does not break it. Other `is-ancestor` uses reviewed and found sound in context: `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh:123`, `infra/scripts/prepare_reclaim_backup.py:129/134` (tracker refs), and the test-suite uses (controlled shas).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 A RED test reproduces the mislabel: a branch whose tip is not an ancestor of main but whose Change-Id IS in main is currently reported `ABANDONED?`.
- [ ] AC2 The detection distinguishes merged-via-rebase from genuinely-not-in-main, and `feature/s1-windows-sweep-probe` (or an equivalent fixture) reports as merged.
- [ ] AC3 No regression in the four branches that already label correctly.
- [ ] AC4 The relationship between `state` and `--delete` is made explicit — either `state` gates deletion, or the script says plainly that deletion is age-driven and `state` is advisory.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (exit 127) — bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Terraform may be written and validated but NEVER applied. Do not touch the shared main checkout; do not `git stash` anywhere.
